correctness.rationale: The longitudinal 2ε inequality and the norm bound at the origin give the stated upper envelope, with transverse error zero at r=0. Turnšek Theorem 1.3 attains the larger-radius branch. For the normalized witness independently checked the junctions, all six pairs of pieces and the limit. Within either tail the squared vertical increment is at most 2D for source distance D; on the middle piece the extra distance is D/r≤1. For the cross-tail pair let a=(r−1)_+, b=√(r+2au)−√r, H=√((r+1)²+2v). If r≤1 then b=0 and the horizontal displacement u+v≥D−1; the upper bound follows from H≤r+1+u+v. If 1≤r≤2, expanding with b²=2au−2√r b gives lower squared slack 4r+2(2−r)v+2(H−√r)b, and the upper bound requires (H−√r)b≤2u+rv. Bound b by au/√r in the constant term and by √(2au) against H−(r+1)≤√(2v); weighted AM–GM gives the claimed inequality since a(√r+1/√r−1+1/r)≤2 on [1,2]. For each mixed pair with a middle point the upper slack follows from convexity in the middle parameter and the two endpoint checks. For the lower bound the horizontal increment suffices when the middle portion is at most one; otherwise the negative-tail expansion has nonnegative terms because k=(r+1)/r≥√r, and the positive-tail expansion is bounded below by 2v(1−u+u/r)+(ku)²−(u−1)² for 1<u≤r, which is nonnegative since 1−u+u/r≥2−r. Thus the all-pairs distortion proof holds for all arguments, including r=1 and r=2. The dyadic asymptote is horizontal because the vertical tail is O(√|t|) and horizontal errors are bounded; the prescribed witness has vertical norm r+1. Scaling by ε preserves the stated conventions. The right limit at zero is over a family of extremizers, not a failure of f(0)=0.
